text: Exam 2 Review Session RAIK 182H: Honors Foundations of Economics Exam Review Questions 2 Review Problem 1. 3 Important Concepts: Taxes and Tax Incidence - The tax is placed on CONSUMERS (i.e. at the register) - ADDS $6 to the sales price (demand curve) - Tax Revenue Box - draw a line up from the new equilibrium (or down if tax on consumers) to the original curve, and over to the y-axis - GRAPH IT. PLEASE - CALCULATE THE Y-INTERCEPTS OF EVERY CURVE AND POINT ON THE TAX BOX - This will help you find tax incidence - how much of the tax each agent pays! 4 Important Concepts: Taxes and Tax Incidence (cont.) - The original equilibrium price “splits” the tax revenue box - Portion above is consumer incidence - Portion below is producer incidence - If it is a $6 tax, the box should be 6 units high - use this to check yourself - If it is, the two incidences should add up to 6 - CS and PS are the triangles above and below the tax box - DWL is the triangle to its right - REMEMBER: Incidence doesn’t change whether you tax producers or consumers! 5 Important Concepts: More on Taxes - People with higher incomes pay higher average tax rate - Progressive System - People with lower incomes pay higher average tax rate - Regressive System - Average tax rates are constant regardless of income - Proportional System - Do you know how tax brackets work? Example? - How would a subsidy be different? - The agent with the more inelastic curve will pay a larger share of the tax 6 Important Concepts: Even More on Taxes - Equity-Efficiency Tradeoff - Public spending as a result of taxes can help promote equity - Taxes are a leaky bucket with deadweight loss, which is an efficiency cost - Making everything fair vs. making the market efficient (closer to perfect comp.) - Government Intervention - Diverting public funds through corruption - Underground or informal economies - Government paternalism 7 Review Problem 2a.- 2c. 8 Important Concepts: Monopoly - The market…? I AM the market. - Legal market power comes from: - Barriers to entry - Patents/Copyrights - Natural market power comes from: - Control of key resources - Economies of scale - Monopolies are price-makers - Goal is to maximize profits by producing where MR = MC! - Profit = PQ - ATC(Q) or (P-ATC) x Q 9 Important Concepts: Monopoly (cont.) - Residual Demand vs. Market Demand - Residual demand curve is for an individual firm - Market demand curve is for an entire market - A monopoly is both! - Can choose quantity and price - A perfectly competitive firm takes what it can get: perfectly elastic residual demand curve 10 Important Concepts: Monopoly (cont.) - Marginal Revenue in a Monopoly - In a perfectly competitive market - MR is flat - In a monopoly - MR is ALWAYS twice the slope of the demand curve - To find this, solve the demand curve for P and double the slope (P) - OR - Solve for total revenue (TR) by solving D for P and multiply by Q (TR = P x Q), then take derivative to find MR 11 Important Concepts: Monopoly (cont.) - Monopoly Pricing - MC is a constant, straight line - Set MR = MC and solve for Q, then plug this Q into the demand curve to find the price - The monopoly is the market, so they can price at their consumers’ willingness to pay rather than just cover their costs (MC) - Mark-up over marginal cost 12 Review Problem 2d.- 2f. 13 Important Concepts: Social “Pie” in Monopoly - Monopolies are wildly inefficient - CS is triangle above the price - PS is the box between the price, MC line, and optimal quantity - DWL is the triangle to the right of the PS box - Price Ceilings - A price ceiling eliminates the ability to price at the willingness to pay, so it’s actually like a “ceiling” now - Extends from the price axis out to the demand curve, then slopes straight downward and rejoins the original MR curve - New PS is the box between the PC price and MC line 14 Important Concepts: Social “Pie” in Monopoly (cont.) - First-Degree Price Discrimination - When price is based on every consumer’s willingness to pay - The entire triangle between D and MC becomes PS - Second-Degree Price Discrimination - Price is based on characteristics of the purchase - Third-Degree Price Discrimination - Price is based on the attribute of the buyer or consumer groups - i.e. age, gender, etc. 15 Important Concepts: Monopolistic Competition - Market structure with many firms and differentiated products - Is competitive because entry/exit is relatively easy - Is monopolistic because firms have a downward- sloping demand curve - Firms can still set prices because there is no perfect substitute for their product - Graph looks just like a monopoly’s! - The only difference is that MC is a curve and the ATC curve will shift to a point of no economic profits in the long-run as firms enter/leave the market when profits/losses are being made 16 Review Problem 3. 17 Important Concepts: Game Theory - The study of strategic interactions - Three elements: - Players, Strategies, Payoffs - Payoff Matrix - Allows you to consider all possible outcomes - Define best responses by thinking about “what-ifs” - i.e. given that my opponent does ___, I will get a higher payoff if I do _____ - Draw the arrows! 18 Important Concepts: Game Theory (cont.) - Dominant Strategy - I will do the same thing no matter what my opponent does - DS Equilibrium: Neither of us want to deviate - Coordination Game: No dominant strategy, we are better off if we can coordinate choices - Prisoner’s Dilemma - Game in which both would be better off if they cooperate, but they can’t credibly agree to do so because they have an incentive to undercut 19 Dominant Strategy Equilibrium 20 Prisoner’s Dilemma 21 Important Concepts: Game Theory (cont.) - Nash Equilibrium - When both players’ best responses point to the same combo of responses - No one wants to change their mind - Pure Strategy vs. Mixed Strategy - Pure: Always choosing the same strategy - Mixed: Randomly choosing based on averages (probability) - These were all simultaneous games! 22 Nash Equilibrium 23 Important Concepts: Extensive Form Games - Sequential Games - Use a game tree - Each point where a decision is made is a node - Use backwards induction to find equilibrium - Analyze Player 2’s decision first, then Player 1’s - First-Mover Advantage - If Player 1 can dictate a better response based on P2’s actions 24 Game Tree 25 Important Concepts: 26 Extensive Form Games - Commitment vs Flexibility - Commitment: i.e. throwing out the steering wheel during Chicken and not being able to change - Flexibility: Any agent can make their move first, no exact order - Collusion - Firms conspire to set quantity or prices - Oligopolies: A few firms compete by setting prices - Grim Strategy: Plan to price at MC forever - If they go lower, they lose money; if higher, no one will buy it Important Concepts: Labor Market - Wage (W) on Y-axis, Worker Hours (H) on the X- axis - Downward-sloping marginal product of labor (MPL) or labor demand curve - Value of MPL: MPL x Output Price - Upward-sloping labor supply curve - Labor-Leisure Tradeoff - The decision between consumption and leisure - Working = $$ = Consumption - Not Working = Leisure - The opportunity cost of leisure is the hourly wage 27 Important Concepts: Labor Market (cont.) - Labor Demand Shifters: 1. Changes in price of output good 2. Changes in technology of firm - Labor-complementing: increase MPL - Labor-saving: decrease MPL - Labor Supply Shifters: 1. Changes in population 2. Changes in workers’ tastes and preferences 3. Changes in opportunity costs 28
